**STEP 2 - Ruler:** The plate is a square-ish white dish about 24 cm across. Vessel area ≈ 3.14 × (12)² ≈ 450 cm².

**STEP 3 - Items:** Roasted broccoli florets (about 6 pieces, some with stems, with dark charred edges). No visible sauce or pooled oil.

**STEP 4 - Area:** The florets cover roughly 20% of the plate (≈ 90 cm²). The rest is empty plate.

**STEP 5 - Volume:** Florets are piled about 2.5 cm high on average, so 90 cm² × 2.5 cm ≈ 225 ml gross envelope.

**STEP 6 - Grams:** Cut vegetables have a bulk density of about 0.5 g/ml, so 225 ml × 0.5 ≈ 110–120 g. I use 120 g.

**STEP 7 - Energy:** Roasted broccoli is about 40 kcal/100 g (raw is about 34 kcal/100 g, plus a little roasting oil and char). 120 g × 40 kcal/100 g ≈ 48 kcal.

**STEP 8 - Sanity check:** Six broccoli florets at about 20 g each is plausible. A small side portion of roughly 120 g and under 50 kcal fits what is visible.
